pack.title: The Silent Sphinx
pack.summary: A real-scale trip across the Giza Plateau: find the four scarabs, learn about the pyramids and the Sphinx, ride a camel, a carriage and a balloon.
intro.story1: For forty-five centuries the Sphinx has watched the sun rise over the Nile. Tonight it went quiet.
intro.story2: Amm Hassan, the oldest camel guide on the plateau, says four blue scarabs keep its voice, and the wind scattered them across the pyramids. Find them, bring them back to the Sphinx, and see what happens.
intro.name: Your name
intro.scale: The plateau is built close to real scale: one metre in the game is one metre in real life.
intro.ctlTouch: Joystick to walk · drag to look · tap someone to talk
intro.ctlDesk: WASD to walk · drag to look · E to interact · click someone to talk
hint.touch: Stick to walk, push all the way to run · Drag to look · Pinch to zoom · Tap the ground to walk there · the gold button changes with what is near you

hint.rideD: WASD to steer · Shift to speed up · E to get off

map.title: Giza Plateau
map.note: Tap anywhere on the map to go there
sphinx.fact: The Great Sphinx was carved from the plateau’s own limestone. It is about 73 m long and 20 m high.
album.caption: Giza Plateau
obj.pyramids: Identify the three Giza pyramids and the kings who built them: Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure.
obj.scale: Describe the size of the Great Pyramid and why its height changed over time.
obj.sphinx: Describe the Great Sphinx: carved from the plateau’s rock and facing east.
obj.crafts: Link materials and crafts to ancient Egypt: papyrus, granite from Aswan and Khufu’s boat.
scarab.all: That is all of them. Take them back to Amm Hassan at the Sphinx.
item.height.q: How tall was the Great Pyramid originally, in metres? (type a number)
item.khufu.q: About how tall was the Great Pyramid when it was finished?
item.khufu.h: Remember what the scarab said: well over 100 metres, but under 200.
item.khafre.q: Why does Khafre's pyramid look taller than Khufu's?
item.khafre.o2: It was built a thousand years later
item.khafre.h: Look at the ground under the two pyramids.
item.menkaure.q: Who built the smallest of the three great pyramids?
item.menkaure.h: You are standing next to that pyramid right now.
item.boat.q: What was found in the sealed pit beside the Great Pyramid in 1954?
item.boat.h: The pit is about 43 metres long… like something that sails on the Nile.
item.sphinx.q: Which direction does the Sphinx face?
item.sphinx.h: It watches the sun rise over the Nile.
item.papyrus.q: What did ancient Egyptians make from the papyrus plant?
item.papyrus.h: Amm Sayed writes names on it in hieroglyphs.
item.granite.q: Where did the red granite of Khafre's Valley Temple come from?
item.granite.h: A place in the south of Egypt, about 800 km away.
hassan.intro.1: Ahlan ya habibi! I'm Hassan. Forty years I've walked camels around these stones, and tonight the Sphinx went quiet.
hassan.intro.2: My grandfather said four blue scarabs keep its voice. The wind scattered them: one at Khufu's north face, one in Khafre's temple, one by Menkaure's little queens, and one at Khufu's boat pit.
hassan.intro.3: The plateau is big, my son, this is real size! If your feet get tired, ride a camel or a carriage. And if you want to see it all at once, Captain Mona has a balloon behind the Valley Temple.
hassan.intro.4: Follow the blue lights in the sky and bring all four back here. Yalla, before the sun sets!
hassan.partial: You have {n} of 4. {hint} The Sphinx is waiting.
hassan.done: Did you see the light show? Bring a friend next time. The plateau is better with company.
finale.1: Ya salaam... all four! Hold them up toward the Sphinx.
finale.2: For four thousand five hundred years I have watched the sun rise over the Nile. Kings came with gold. Travelers came with questions.
finale.3: You came with four small scarabs and very tired feet. That is enough. I will speak again.
finale.4: Go, Guardian of Giza. The stones will light up for you tonight. Bring your friends to see them.
abu.1: Ahlan! Shai bel na'na'? The best mint tea in Nazlet el-Semman.
abu.done: They say you woke the Sphinx. Tea is free for guardians, ya basha.
abu.all: You have all four scarabs! Hurry to the Sphinx, Amm Hassan is waiting.
tea.done: You drank mint tea! You will run faster for a minute and a half.
sayed.1: Ahlan! Papyrus is a plant that grew along the Nile, and ancient Egyptians made paper from it about five thousand years ago. Shall I write your name in hieroglyphs inside a cartouche, like a king?
mona.1: Ahlan, captain! In real life Egypt’s balloon flights take off in Luxor at sunrise, but today we have a special flight over Giza. Up fires the burner, Down lets you sink. Try to fly through all six golden rings.
fathi.1: Licorice, cool and fresh! Sellers clack these brass cymbals so people hear them coming from far away.
tourist.0: Wow! The pyramid is much bigger than I imagined.
tourist.1: They say the Great Pyramid has about 2.3 million blocks. Who counted them?!
tourist.2: Could someone take my photo? The light is perfect right now.
tourist.3: I came from the other side of the world just to see the Sphinx!
tourist.4: Sunset here is like a dream.
scarab.khufu.lore: The Great Pyramid rose about 146 metres when it was finished, around 2560 BC. For more than 3,800 years nothing built by people stood taller.
scarab.khafre.lore: Khafre's pyramid looks taller than his father Khufu's because it stands on higher ground. Near its tip you can still see the smooth white casing stones that once covered all three pyramids.
scarab.menkaure.lore: Menkaure built the smallest of the three great pyramids, originally about 65 metres high. The three little pyramids beside it are known as the Queens’ Pyramids.
scarab.boat.lore: In 1954 a sealed pit here held Khufu's cedar boat, about 43 metres long, taken apart into more than a thousand pieces. In 2021 it was moved, whole, to the Grand Egyptian Museum.
scarab.got: The scarab glows in your hand! {hint}
card.area.khufu: The Great Pyramid is about 230 m along each side and was 146.6 m tall. Today it is about 138 m, because its tip and smooth casing stones were taken away. The pole on top shows how high the original tip reached.
card.area.khafre: Khafre’s pyramid is about 215 m wide and was originally 143.5 m tall. Its sides are a little steeper than Khufu’s, so it looks sharper.
card.area.menkaure: See the big gash in the north face of Menkaure’s pyramid? In 1196 a ruler tried to tear the pyramids down. His workers dug for months, then gave up and left only this scar.
card.area.queens-k: These small pyramids were built for King Khufu’s queens. Most of their outer stone was taken away over the centuries.
card.area.west: These mastabas are tombs of officials and nobles from the age of the pyramid builders. "Mastaba" is the Arabic word for a bench, which is what they look like.
card.area.sphinx: The Sphinx is about 73 m long and 20 m high, carved from the plateau’s own rock, and it faces due east. Its nose has been broken for centuries, and a piece of its beard is in the British Museum in London.
card.area.valley: Khafre’s Valley Temple has limestone walls cased in red granite blocks brought from Aswan, about 800 km away.
card.area.nazlet: Nazlet el-Semman is a village at the edge of the plateau. Its families have worked with horses, camels and visitors for generations.
card.area.pano: From Panorama Point you can see all three pyramids lined up in one view. Find the golden marker and take a photo!
veh.zaghloul.line: Zaghloul chews slowly and stares at you. He does not do free rides… but today he will make an exception.
veh.fayrouz.line: Fayrouz is wearing more tassels than anyone on the plateau, and she knows it.
veh.bondok.line: Bondok sniffs your pockets for dates. You have none. He is disappointed.
veh.shams.line: Shams stares at the pyramid as if she is counting the stones.
ring.all: All six rings! You are a natural pilot.
card.ring.0: From above, the Great Pyramid’s base is almost a perfect square: its longest and shortest sides differ by only centimetres.
card.ring.1: Khafre’s sides slope at about 53 degrees, Khufu’s at about 52. A small difference you can see from up here.
card.ring.2: Menkaure’s pyramid has only about a tenth of the Great Pyramid’s volume.
card.ring.3: The Sphinx faces due east, toward the sunrise over the Nile.
card.ring.4: From above Nazlet el-Semman you can see how Cairo has grown right up to the foot of the plateau.
card.ring.5: Look northwest: that is the Grand Egyptian Museum, one of the largest museums in the world devoted to a single civilisation, home to Tutankhamun’s treasures.

cart.title: Your name in a cartouche
cart.note: This is a playful, approximate spelling: each sign stands for a sound close to a letter in your name. A cartouche is the oval ancient Egyptians drew around royal names.
cart.empty: I could not write that name. Try a name in Arabic or English letters.
